title: The Community Survey: What the Numbers Really Say · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: Last month, a group of volunteers in the town of Greenfield carried out a survey about local shopping habits. The group wanted to know how often people shopped in the town centre and what they thought of the local market. They printed 500 questionnaires and gave them out on a Saturday morning outside the main supermarket. By the end of the day, they had collected 320 completed forms. The volunteers were pleased with the number of responses. However, when they began to analyse the data, they noticed several problems. First, most of the people who answered the survey were older residents. Only 18 per cent of the respondents were under 30 years old. The volunteers knew that younger people often shop online, so the survey may not represent the whole town. Second, the questions were not always clear. One question asked, “How often do you visit the town centre?”
prompt:
Part 1
Do you often look at numbers or charts in your daily life?
Have you ever answered a survey? What was it about?
Do you think surveys are useful? Why or why not?
When you see a chart, what do you look at first?

Part 2
Describe a time when you saw a chart or a set of numbers that surprised you. You should say: where you saw it; what the numbers were about; why it surprised you; and explain what you learned from it.

Part 3
Why do some surveys give unreliable results?
How can companies make their surveys better?
Do you think people always tell the truth in surveys? Why?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of online surveys?
